application_guidance.input_pattern: A nonempty compact geodesically convex K containing the intended minimizer p.
read_original_when: Dropping compactness, changing the ambient geometry or changing the radial source.
sensitive_conditions: The global extension is defined by a minimum over K, not an arbitrary ambient infimum.
Agreement on K and the positive distance floor require the stated mu range.
Oracle realization needs additional supporting-contact conditions; model membership alone is not a Hard Family.

imported_interfaces.reading: Statement and source proof read: second variation has nonnegative integrand under curvature -1; continuity and ordered one-sided slopes extend convexity through endpoint coincidences.
imported_interfaces.statement: Distance in H^d is jointly convex along pairs of constant-speed geodesics.

content.intended_use: Prove global model membership, minimizer uniqueness and distance-to-objective-error conversion for a carrier objective.

proofs.full_local_argument: For fixed y the minimized expression is continuous on nonempty compact K, hence has a minimizer. Given y0,y1 choose minimizers x0,x1. Let yt and xt be the constant-speed geodesics joining the respective pairs, with common t in [0,1]. Convexity of K gives xt in K. Joint convexity of distance, including the constant geodesic p, yields F(yt)<=mu d(xt,p)+d(yt,xt)<=(1-t)[mu d(x0,p)+d(y0,x0)]+t[mu d(x1,p)+d(y1,x1)]=(1-t)F(y0)+tF(y1). For arbitrary y,w and a minimizer x_w, the triangle inequality gives F(y)<=mu d(x_w,p)+d(y,x_w)<=F(w)+d(y,w); exchange y,w to obtain |F(y)-F(w)|<=d(y,w). For every x in K, d(x,p)>=d(y,p)-d(y,x), so mu d(x,p)+d(y,x)>=mu d(y,p)+(1-mu)d(y,x)>=mu d(y,p). Taking the minimum proves the floor. If y in K, the choice x=y gives the reverse bound F(y)<=mu d(y,p), hence equality on K. In particular F(p)=0. If y is not p, the floor is strictly positive because mu>0, proving uniqueness.
map: Interpolate evaluation points and minimizing contacts, using joint convexity of distance.
Triangle inequalities give Lipschitzness, the floor and agreement on K.
proofs.omitted_details: The joint-convexity interface is imported explicitly from the read Lemma5.1; it is not claimed as a new independently proved geometry theorem.
proofs.reading_coverage: Direct original-PDF pp.8–9 and supplied images inspected; complete Lemma5.3 statement and proof read.

assumptions: K is nonempty, compact and geodesically convex.
0<mu<1; mu is a radial weight, not a strong-convexity modulus.
statement.conclusion: The minimum is attained. F_{K,p} is globally geodesically convex and globally 1-Lipschitz. F_{K,p}(y)>=mu d(y,p), F_{K,p}(p)=0, and p is its unique global minimizer. For every y in K, F_{K,p}(y)=mu d(y,p).
statement.objects_and_definitions: On finite-dimensional curvature -1 hyperbolic space H^d with geodesic distance d, define F_{K,p}(y)=min_{x in K}{mu d(x,p)+d(y,x)}.
statement.parameter_domains: Finite dimension; 0<mu<1; y ranges over the entire ambient space.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such K,p,mu, all conclusions hold simultaneously for every y in H^d; no randomization or Oracle is involved.

use_restrictions: Complete local argument is proposed for independent checking; no Reviewer result is asserted.
Does not by itself establish any Oracle lower bound.

facets.subject: Nonempty compact geodesically convex K in H^d, p in K, 0<mu<1

research_use.reason: Convert a controlled carrier into an ambient objective while retaining an explicit minimizer and error floor.

summary: A compact convex carrier extends its radial source to a globally geodesically convex 1-Lipschitz objective with a unique minimizer and a global distance floor.
title: Bounded convex carrier extension, Lemma 5.3
use_when: Construct a globally valid objective from a radial source on a compact geodesically convex carrier; this lemma alone does not give hardness.
